acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Harpies family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Matriarch, T4, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Plumage-Court Champion (Champion) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Ceremonial plumage forms a cloak around vivid wings, gold ankle rings cap the talons, the crest becomes elaborate, and hair is braided with trophy feathers.
Signature mechanic: Ceremonial Mantle: the Matriarch wraps cloak-like plumage around one lower Harpy, then rotates the flock one quarter-turn and attacks from the open side with the opposite talon.
battlefieldDuty: Marshal a rotating flock formation, protecting one lower flyer with ceremonial plumage while attacking from the opposite edge.
constructionDimensions: Tier-safe attachments: T1–T3 bind shale feather caps, mineral weights, and breakaway talon sheaths with bone beads and rawhide straps at talons or wing roots; T4–T5 seat the same loads in reinforced gold ankle rings and gold cuffs without granting rank ornaments to earlier forms.
Locomotion alternates between weighted glides and hard stone perches: dust falls from loaded feathers, talons lock into visible cracks, and pale fracture seams open in the active weight or sheath.
counterplay: Move opposite the raised ring, separate the sheltered flyer, or strike the trailing wing before the rotation completes. Affinity signal: T1–T3 drop a rawhide-strapped talon weight whose crack turns pale before descent; T4–T5 release the weight from a gold ankle ring or gold cuff, and breaking either tier's visible mount forces a slow relaunch.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only brown plumage without mineral load paths and changed flight behavior
Glow-only earth treatment without weight, fractures, or breakaway stone construction
Solid rock wings that could not fold or fly
Boulder effects that conceal the raptor anatomy
identityInvariants: A humanoid torso remains joined to large raptor wings that replace or extend the arms, backward-jointed bird legs, oversized talons, and a feathered head crest.
Slate grey, brown, and dirty cream mature into iridescent blue-green, storm purple, and white without losing the family feather pattern.
Feather, hollow bone, sinew, raw hide, braided hair, and gold ankle ornaments remain physically readable materials.
Bone jewelry, trophy feathers, braided hair, ankle rings, and crest height communicate status without changing the core wing-and-talon silhouette.
Every attack keeps the wing roots, talons, crest, and flight direction visible enough to preserve counterplay.
telegraph: Its elaborate crest leans toward the protected flyer, one gold ankle ring lifts, and braided trophy feathers sweep around that side.
